title: Oedipus Rex, Sophocles
subtitle: 5th century BC
subject: litterature
description: Oedipus wants to save Thebes from a plague. As he investigates, he discovers that he is the guilty man. Sophocles invents the tragedy in which knowing means destroying yourself.

hero.hook: He hunts the city's murderer. The murderer is him.

blocks.text: In Athens, in the **5th century BC**, the playwright **Sophocles** created **Oedipus Rex**. **Aristotle**, the Greek philosopher and student of Plato, would later call it the model of perfect tragedy in his **Poetics**. In one evening of theater, a king runs an investigation. Every answer brings him closer to the abyss.

The city of **Thebes** is struck by a plague. The **oracle**, the answer of the gods delivered at the sanctuary of Delphi, demands that the murderer of the old king **Laius** be punished. **Oedipus**, the current king of Thebes, promises to find him. He does not yet know that fate has already placed him at the center of the crime.

Before Sophocles, Athenian tragedy was already changing with **Aeschylus**, the first of the three great tragedians. Sophocles refined the form: more characters, more psychological tension. He introduced the **tritagonist**, the third actor on stage. The **chorus** accompanies the action and comments on it. But the real engine is a man facing what he does not know.

blocks.caption: Oedipus before the Sphinx: solving the riddle is already stepping into the trap

blocks.text: The myth of Oedipus was known before the play. Everyone remembered the **Sphinx**, a monster with a woman's head and a lion's body. Its **ainigma**, the Greek word for “riddle,” asked: “Which animal walks on four legs in the morning, two at noon, and three in the evening?” Oedipus answers: man. He becomes king of Thebes. Sophocles does not surprise us with the plot alone. He surprises us with the way the hero uncovers the truth **in public**, step by step, unable to stop.

sections.title: The investigation that turns on the investigator

blocks.text: Oedipus questions the seer [[Tiresias]], the blind prophet of Thebes who sees both past and future. Then he questions his wife **Jocasta**, the widow of Laius. The clues pile up. The man he killed on a road, the woman he married, the children he fathered: everything matches the oracle he thought he had escaped by leaving Corinth, the city where he believed he had grown up.
Aristotle admired two effects in this play above all: the [[peripeteia]], the sudden reversal of fortune, and the [[anagnorisis]], the moment when Oedipus finally understands who he is.

This is **tragic irony**: the harder Oedipus tries to be just and clear-sighted, the faster he falls. Knowledge does not soothe. It burns. Every question asked in the name of the city brings the king nearer his own sentence. Sophocles shows that a brilliant mind can become the instrument of its own ruin.

sections.title: Seeing too clearly, then going blind

blocks.text: When the truth breaks out, Jocasta kills herself. Oedipus puts out his own eyes. The king who could see for the whole city becomes a man who refuses to look at the world. Sophocles ties together [[Fate and free will in Greek tragedy]]: Oedipus acted freely at every step, and yet every step carried out the oracle. Running from fate sometimes means fulfilling it.

blocks.caption: The riddle of the Sphinx: the knowledge that saves Thebes sets up the disaster

blocks.text: The plague, the [[loimos]], was not only a disease. It was the religious pollution that strikes a city as punishment for a crime. Oedipus becomes the [[pharmakos]], the scapegoat driven out to purify the city. He leaves Thebes as a beggar, carrying the evil he never knew he had done.

sections.title: From Freud to our modern whodunits

blocks.text: In the 20th century, **Freud**, the founder of psychoanalysis, read the [[Oedipus complex (Freud)]] into the myth. That psychoanalytic concept sits a long way from what Sophocles was thinking about, which was fate. Beyond psychoanalysis, the play remains the model of the investigation in which the detective discovers that he is the culprit. Crime novels, theater, film: the structure still holds.

**Oedipus Rex** shows that you can want the good of everyone and wreck your own life while looking for the truth. In Sophocles, seeing clearly is not a victory. It is an ordeal that leaves the city saved and the man broken.
